prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t name one single “best” firm for everyone, because the right choice depends on your exact location, roof type, budget and whether you need help with an insurance claim. I can, however, tell you how to find the best hurricane‑rated roof contractor in Miami and offer to pull a short vetted list for your ZIP if you want.

What I need from you (optional)
- ZIP code or street address (so I can narrow to local contractors)
- Residential or commercial roof
- Roof material wanted (shingles, metal, tile, TPO, etc.) or open to options
- Whether this is an insurance claim or private pay

How to identify the best hurricane‑rated roof contractor (checklist)
1. Proper licensing and insurance
   - Verify the contractor’s Florida license on the DBPR site (Department of Business & Professional Regulation).
   - Ask for current general liability and workers’ comp certificates and confirm they’re active.

2. Miami‑Dade / FL product and installation compliance
   - Insist on materials that have Miami‑Dade County Approval (NOA) for hurricane protection.
   - Contractor should be familiar with high‑velocity hurricane zone (HVHZ) requirements and local building code.
   - Request engineered wind‑load calculations and attachment details (clips, straps, fastener schedules).

3. Manufacturer certifications and warranties
   - Look for GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed, TAMKO, or metal‑roof manufacturer certifications.
   - Confirm both manufacturer warranty and contractor workmanship/installation warranty in writing.

4. Experience with hurricane/weather‑resistant systems
   - Ask for examples and references of recent hurricane‑rated installations in Miami (photos, names you can call).
   - Prefer contractors who have worked on similar roof types and in your neighborhood’s HVHZ.

5. Good reputation and local presence
   - Check Google Reviews, Better Business Bureau, Angi/Houzz and local Facebook groups.
   - Local offices and staff matter — post‑storm responsiveness is important.

6. Transparent written proposal and permitting
   - Get a detailed written estimate with materials, brand/model, scope, timeline, permit responsibility, cleanup, and payment schedule.
   - Contractor should pull required permits and arrange inspections.

7. Insurance‑claim experience (if applicable)
   - If you’re filing a claim, pick a contractor experienced in working with insurers and preparing scope/damage reports.
   - Avoid contractors who pressure you to sign over insurance checks or demand large upfront payments.

Typical questions to ask a contractor
- Are you licensed in Florida? Can I see your DBPR number?
- Are you certified by the material manufacturer? Which ones?
- Do you use products with Miami‑Dade NOA? Can you provide the NOA numbers?
- What is included in your workmanship warranty? Length?
- Will you pull permits and handle inspections?
- Can you provide at least three local references from similar jobs?

If you want, I can:
- Look up and shortlist 3–5 highly rated Miami roofing contractors (I’ll need your ZIP).
- Provide a checklist template and email/phone script to use when you call them.
- Review 2–3 written estimates if you paste them here.

Which option would you like?
